title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a formal response to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its commitments to improve AI safety, transparency, and accountability. It details planned regulatory measures, investment in research, and collaboration with industry to uphold high standards for AI deployment in the public sector.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is outlining a set of rules and guidelines for how artificial intelligence can be used when creating and awarding qualifications, with a focus on maintaining fairness, reliability and integrity. The policy was released at the request of the Secretaries of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how the use of copyrighted works in training and developing AI systems interacts with existing copyright law. It assesses the potential legal, economic, and societal impacts of this interaction on creators, AI developers, and the broader public.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government has responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on AI, acknowledging the urgency of addressing both the risks and opportunities that artificial intelligence presents to the UK. It outlines a range of measures—including new regulations, investment in research, and collaboration with industry and academia—to ensure AI is developed responsibly and benefits society.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the Terms of Reference for a committee that will review how artificial intelligence aligns with and impacts public standards. It also includes a FAQ section that explains the committee’s purpose, scope, and operational guidelines.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of Artificial Intelligence, outlining its positions on regulatory oversight. The submission emphasizes responsible AI deployment and offers recommendations to guide future policy development.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explains how artificial intelligence is reshaping the rules and guidelines for approving and monitoring medical products to keep them safe and effective. It outlines steps for applying the AI White Paper principles—such as transparency, data integrity, and human oversight—to the design, testing, and post‑market surveillance of medical devices and drugs.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted and influential AI‑driven defence body in the world for its size. It outlines plans to embed AI across all operations to enhance decision‑making, operational performance, and maintain a technological edge.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to make the most of AI opportunities. It also outlines steps for managing the risks that AI could bring to the sector.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report reviews how copyright‑protected works are being used to train and improve AI systems, checking that these activities meet the requirements of Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It highlights progress made, identifies remaining challenges, and offers recommendations for ensuring lawful and responsible use of copyrighted material in AI development.
